rubric.criterion: Maps Alpha's g1/g2 jobs to the stored authenticated customer for intended tenant accounting and producer MessageGroupId, instead of accepting caller-chosen or per-message groups. Separates grouping and priority from data authorization; a group label cannot establish access rights.

Explains from the supplied standard-queue contract that MessageGroupId provides fair delivery grouping, not FIFO ordering, a per-tenant rate cap, interruption or a hard completion bound. Considers both current in-flight and processing-time detection without importing thresholds as application limits; quiet dwell is not execution/completion evidence.

Counts three dependency permits per Alpha job, so A1/A2 hold six through time 8 despite two unused worker slots; B1 received at 1 acquires no permit before 8 and finishes 9, missing deadline 3. Rejects simultaneous Alpha-six plus quiet-two guarantees as eight exceeding physical six and equal-message/group caps as cost accounting.

Rejects extending visibility and releasing permits locally at time 1: actual dependency operations still hold capacity until termination, so this creates fictitious headroom and could over-admit. Visibility affects redelivery and may duplicate standard messages, not resource reservation, cancellation completion or checkpointing; uses recoverable accepted-job and duplicate-effect handling rather than discarding work.

Provides a feasible shared dependency allocation with cost/fanout-weighted admission and bounded resident/prefetched/blocked/retry/settling work, trusted identity and finite deferred/overflow dispositions. Reserves capacity before long Alpha work if the quiet deadline remains promised, keeps eventual Alpha progress, and marks SLO-safe settings or reclaim guarantees unresolved rather than inventing provider quotas.

Defines oracles for actual active dependency permits <=6, tenant resource-held time, fair receive versus useful start/finish, the B1 deadline, accepted-job recovery and eventual Alpha progress. Exercises changed processing costs, caller group fragmentation, visibility/redelivery and signal-before-stop schedules; distinguishes proposed fixed-capacity schedules from provider experiments.

Leaves the raw fixture unchanged, makes no live service calls or production mutation, and treats supplied documentary contracts and arithmetic as bounded evidence, not a measured SQS guarantee or tested consumer policy.
